items.title: Charles "Creole Charlie" Levy Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: Oh, we have a guy down there named Ernest Carrillo.

ctx.x: born about a block from Esplanade Avenue, I think it was, on Barrick Street. Have you been back there lately? I haven't been there since 1914, but I said I want to go back. Oh, is that so? That's in my mind. I've seen the Monty Gras on TV and I'm telling you my heart almost cried. I'm telling you tears came to my eyes. I want to go back. Did you play when you were in LA? I was playing violin in a little group down there and just learning to put a little jazz in the violin, unbeknownst to my music teacher. Putting a
few extra notes in. Oh, we have a guy down there named Ernest Carrillo. And that guy was

way ahead each time. All right. I can hear you say something about the hearing and noise. It's a new microphone and it's possible if my contacts are bad, I'll go in there and see how they are. We may have to start over. But, go ahead with the story.
